9. [Maximum mark: 14]

A quadratic function f can be written in the form f(x) = a(x − p)(x − 3). The graph of f has axis of symmetry x = 2.5 and y-intercept at (0, −6).

(a) Find the value of p. [3]

(b) Find the value of a. [3]

(c) The line y = kx − 5 is a tangent to the curve of f. Find the values of k. [8]
records.independentSolutionText: The roots are p and 3, whose midpoint is 2.5, so (p+3)/2=2.5 and p=2. Since f(0)=a(−2)(−3)=6a=−6, a=−1. Thus f(x)=−(x−2)(x−3)=−x²+5x−6. Intersections with y=kx−5 satisfy −x²+5x−6=kx−5, or x²+(k−5)x+1=0. Tangency requires discriminant zero: (k−5)²−4=0, so k−5=±2 and k=3 or 7.
